rounds.statement: \begin{gathered}\textnormal{Let measurable f:[0,1] to}\\\textnormal{[0,1] satisfy}\\\operatorname{length}\{x:f(x)>t\}=1-t^{1/3}\ (0<t<1).\\\textnormal{Find (minimum, maximum) of}\\\int_0^1x f(x)\,dx.\end{gathered}
solution: \begin{gathered}\textnormal{Layer cake reduces each level}\\\textnormal{set to a set of prescribed}\\\textnormal{length.}\end{gathered}
\begin{gathered}\textnormal{Placing every level set on the}\\\textnormal{left minimizes the moment;}\\\textnormal{placing it on the right}\\\textnormal{maximizes it.}\end{gathered}
\begin{gathered}\textnormal{Use the branch with positive}\\\textnormal{real part and then take real}\\\textnormal{parts.}\end{gathered}
\begin{gathered}\textnormal{Integration by parts controls}\\\textnormal{the oscillatory tail, so the}\\\textnormal{regulator limit equals the}\\\textnormal{improper integral.}\end{gathered}
\begin{gathered}\textnormal{Differentiate in b, then use}\\\textnormal{x=b/(a t) in the derivative}\\\textnormal{integral.}\end{gathered}
